entries.notes: image of ……的图像或印象；public image 公众形象；mental image 脑海中的画面；be the image of 与……十分相像。image 不等同于 imagination 想象力。

senses.definitionEn: A visual representation, photograph, or reflected likeness.

example.en: The mirror produced a clear image.
example.zh: 镜子映出了清晰的影像。

senses.definitionEn: The general impression others have of a person or organization.

example.en: The company wants to improve its image.
example.zh: 公司希望改善自身形象。

senses.definitionEn: A picture formed in the mind.

example.en: The story created a vivid image in my mind.
example.zh: 这个故事在我脑海中形成了生动的画面。

senses.definitionEn: A word or description that creates a vivid comparison or picture.

example.en: The poem uses images of light and darkness.
example.zh: 这首诗运用了光明与黑暗的意象。

senses.definitionEn: To produce a picture or digital copy of something.

example.en: The scanner images the inside of the body.
example.zh: 扫描仪对人体内部进行成像。

entries.orderingBasis: 继承 Sites 第17版顺序；无客观词频声明；待词典与人工核对

entries.notes: universal access 人人可及；universal agreement 普遍共识；universal truth 普遍真理；universal charger 通用充电器。“普遍”有时是概括，并非精确统计的所有。

senses.definitionEn: Existing everywhere or shared by everyone in a group.

example.en: The desire for safety is universal.
example.zh: 对安全的渴望是普遍的。

senses.definitionEn: Relating to the whole world or all people.

example.en: The declaration sets out universal human rights.
example.zh: 该宣言阐明了普遍人权。

senses.definitionEn: Suitable for many different uses or systems.

example.en: This is a universal remote control.
example.zh: 这是一个通用遥控器。

senses.definitionEn: A general property or concept shared by particular things.

example.en: The course examines the problem of universals.
example.zh: 这门课探讨共相问题。

entries.notes: strain 与 stress 有重叠；材料力学中 stress 是应力，strain 是应变。strain a muscle 拉伤肌肉；put a strain on 给……造成负担。

senses.definitionEn: Pressure that stretches someone's resources or endurance.

example.en: The extra work put a strain on her.
example.zh: 额外工作给她造成了负担。

senses.definitionEn: To injure a muscle by stretching it too much; such an injury.

example.en: He strained a muscle in his back.
example.zh: 他拉伤了背部肌肉。

senses.definitionEn: A variety of an organism or a particular type.

example.en: Researchers identified a new strain of the virus.
example.zh: 研究人员识别出一种新的病毒株。

senses.definitionEn: To make a great effort or stretch something tightly.

example.en: I strained to hear the announcement.
example.zh: 我竭力听清广播。

senses.definitionEn: To separate liquid from solids using a filter.

example.en: Strain the soup before serving.
example.zh: 上桌前把汤过滤一下。

senses.definitionEn: The sound of a tune or passage of music.

example.en: We heard the strains of a violin.
example.zh: 我们听到了小提琴的旋律。

senses.definitionEn: Deformation measured relative to original size.

example.en: The gauge measures strain in the metal.
example.zh: 仪器测量金属中的应变。

entries.orderingBasis: 继承 Sites 第17版顺序；无客观词频声明；待词典与人工核对

entries.notes: bound 有多个来源：bind—bound—bound（捆绑）；bound 作跳跃用规则变化 bounded；be bound to do 必定/很可能；be bound for 前往；be bound by 受约束。

senses.definitionEn: Certain or very likely to do something, used with to.

example.en: You are bound to make mistakes at first.
example.zh: 你刚开始很可能会犯错。

senses.definitionEn: Travelling toward a particular destination.

example.en: This train is bound for Beijing.
example.zh: 这列火车开往北京。

senses.definitionEn: Tied, fastened, or joined, as a form of bind.

example.en: The books were bound in leather.
example.zh: 这些书用皮革装订。

senses.definitionEn: Required by duty, law, or an agreement.

example.en: We are bound by the contract.
example.zh: 我们受合同约束。

senses.definitionEn: A limit or boundary.

example.en: His enthusiasm knows no bounds.
example.zh: 他的热情无穷无尽。

senses.definitionEn: To move with large jumps; a long jump.

example.en: The dog bounded across the field.
example.zh: 狗蹦跳着穿过田野。

senses.definitionEn: To form a boundary around something.

example.en: The garden is bounded by a low wall.
example.zh: 花园以一道矮墙为界。

entries.orderingBasis: 继承 Sites 第17版顺序；无客观词频声明；待词典与人工核对

entries.notes: a rock band 摇滚乐队；a band of 一群；a rubber band 橡皮筋；band together 联合起来；bandwidth 带宽。

senses.definitionEn: A group of musicians who perform together.

example.en: She plays guitar in a band.
example.zh: 她在一个乐队里弹吉他。

senses.definitionEn: A strip or loop of material.

example.en: She tied the papers with a rubber band.
example.zh: 她用橡皮筋捆住文件。

senses.definitionEn: A group of people sharing an activity or purpose.

example.en: A band of volunteers cleaned the beach.
example.zh: 一群志愿者清理了海滩。

senses.definitionEn: A range of values, frequencies, or categories.

example.en: The job falls within a higher pay band.
example.zh: 这份工作属于较高的薪酬等级。

senses.definitionEn: A stripe of colour or contrasting material.

example.en: The snake has yellow bands.
example.zh: 这条蛇身上有黄色条纹。

senses.definitionEn: To fasten with a band or join together as a group.

example.en: Local families banded together to help.
example.zh: 当地家庭联合起来提供帮助。

entries.orderingBasis: 继承 Sites 第17版顺序；无客观词频声明；待词典与人工核对

entries.notes: in line 排队；on the line 在线上、面临风险；in line with 与……一致；line up 排队；draw the line 划清界限；bottom line 底线或最终结果。

senses.definitionEn: A long narrow mark, edge, or wrinkle.

example.en: Draw a straight line.
example.zh: 画一条直线。

senses.definitionEn: A row of written words or a sentence spoken in a play.

example.en: The actor forgot his lines.
example.zh: 那位演员忘词了。

senses.definitionEn: A row of people or things, especially a queue.

example.en: We waited in line for tickets.
example.zh: 我们排队等着买票。

senses.definitionEn: A route or connection for transport or communication.

example.en: The phone line is busy.
example.zh: 电话占线。

senses.definitionEn: A dividing boundary or a position taken on an issue.

example.en: The river marks the line between the two regions.
example.zh: 这条河是两个地区的分界线。

senses.definitionEn: A field of work or range of related products.

example.en: The company launched a new line of shoes.
example.zh: 公司推出了一个新的鞋类系列。

senses.definitionEn: A length of cord, or a chain of descent.

example.en: His family line goes back centuries.
example.zh: 他的家族血统可追溯数百年。

senses.definitionEn: To form a row along the edge or sides of something.

example.en: Trees line both sides of the road.
example.zh: 道路两旁树木成行。

senses.definitionEn: To cover the inside of something with a layer of material.

example.en: Line the tin with baking paper.
example.zh: 在烤模内铺上烘焙纸。

entries.orderingBasis: 继承 Sites 第17版顺序；无客观词频声明；待词典与人工核对

entries.notes: lean—leaned/leant；lean against 靠着；lean toward(s) 倾向于；lean on 倚靠、依赖，也可指施压。lean meat 瘦肉；lean management 精益管理。

senses.definitionEn: To bend from an upright position or rest against something.

example.en: He leaned against the wall.
example.zh: 他倚靠着墙。

senses.definitionEn: To depend on someone or pressure them, used with on.

example.en: You can lean on your friends for support.
example.zh: 你可以依靠朋友获得支持。

senses.definitionEn: To be inclined toward an opinion or choice.

example.en: I lean towards the cheaper option.
example.zh: 我倾向于较便宜的方案。

senses.definitionEn: Thin and fit, or containing little fat.

example.en: Choose lean meat for this dish.
example.zh: 做这道菜要选瘦肉。

senses.definitionEn: Using only necessary resources and avoiding waste.

example.en: They run a lean organization.
example.zh: 他们管理着一个精简高效的组织。

senses.definitionEn: Having little money, food, or other resources.

example.en: The family faced several lean years.
example.zh: 这家人度过了几年拮据的日子。

senses.definitionEn: An inclination in position or preference.

example.en: The tower has a noticeable lean.
example.zh: 这座塔明显倾斜。

entries.orderingBasis: 继承 Sites 第17版顺序；无客观词频声明；待词典与人工核对

entries.notes: post a letter 寄信（英式）；a job post 职位；post a message 发消息；keep sb posted 让某人随时了解情况；post-war 战后的（post- 前缀“之后”）。

senses.definitionEn: An item published on a website or social platform.

example.en: I read your latest post.
example.zh: 我看了你最新的帖子。

senses.definitionEn: A job or a place where someone is assigned to work.

example.en: He accepted a teaching post.
example.zh: 他接受了一个教师职位。

senses.definitionEn: The system of sending letters or the letters delivered.

example.en: The parcel arrived in the morning post.
example.zh: 包裹随早上的邮件送到了。

senses.definitionEn: To send by mail or publish information publicly.

example.en: She posted a message online.
example.zh: 她在网上发布了一条消息。

senses.definitionEn: An upright piece of wood or metal.

example.en: The ball hit the goalpost.
example.zh: 球击中了球门柱。

senses.definitionEn: To assign someone to a place or display a notice.

example.en: A guard was posted at the entrance.
example.zh: 入口处安排了一名警卫。

senses.definitionEn: To report financial results or enter a transaction in an account.

example.en: The company posted a profit this year.
example.zh: 公司公布今年实现盈利。

entries.orderingBasis: 继承 Sites 第17版顺序；无客观词频声明；待词典与人工核对

entries.notes: a quarter of 四分之一；a quarter past six 六点一刻；a quarter to six 差一刻六点；quarters 表住所，headquarters 总部。

senses.definitionEn: One of four equal parts, or fifteen minutes.

example.en: A quarter of the class was absent.
example.zh: 班里四分之一的学生缺席。

senses.definitionEn: A three-month business period or one of four parts of a game.

example.en: Sales rose in the first quarter.
example.zh: 第一季度销售额增长了。

senses.definitionEn: A coin worth twenty-five cents.

example.en: The machine takes quarters.
example.zh: 这台机器接收二十五美分硬币。

senses.meaningZh: 城区；区域；某一方面的人士
senses.definitionEn: A district of a town, or a source of opinion or support.

example.en: We walked through the old quarter.
example.zh: 我们步行穿过老城区。

senses.definitionEn: Rooms or buildings used as accommodation.

example.en: The staff quarters are behind the hotel.
example.zh: 员工宿舍在酒店后面。

senses.meaningZh: 把……分成四份；为……安排住宿
senses.definitionEn: To divide into four parts or provide accommodation.

example.en: Quarter the apples before cooking.
example.zh: 烹煮前把苹果切成四块。

senses.definitionEn: Mercy shown to a defeated opponent.

example.en: The commander ordered his men to give no quarter.
example.zh: 指挥官命令士兵不要饶恕敌人。

entries.orderingBasis: 继承 Sites 第17版顺序；无客观词频声明；待词典与人工核对

entries.notes: fix a bug 修复程序错误；a stomach bug 常指引起肠胃不适的感染；stop bugging me 是口语“别烦我了”。

senses.definitionEn: A small insect or similar tiny creature.

example.en: A little bug landed on my sleeve.
example.zh: 一只小虫落在我的袖子上。

senses.definitionEn: An error in software that causes unexpected behavior.

example.en: The update fixes a bug that made the app crash.
example.zh: 这次更新修复了一个会让应用崩溃的错误。

senses.definitionEn: A minor illness caused by an infection.

example.en: I think I picked up a stomach bug.
example.zh: 我想我可能得了肠胃炎。

senses.definitionEn: To annoy someone, especially repeatedly.

example.en: It bugs me when people talk during the film.
example.zh: 电影放映时有人说话会让我很烦。

senses.definitionEn: A hidden listening device, or to put one in a place.

example.en: They found a bug under the desk.
example.zh: 他们在桌子下面发现了一个窃听器。

entries.orderingBasis: 优先排列常见用法，再列语域或专业义项。

entries.notes: look forward to 中的 to 是介词，后接名词或动名词，如 look forward to seeing you；forward an email to sb 是把邮件转发给某人。

senses.definitionEn: Towards a position in front.

example.en: She leaned forward to hear him better.
example.zh: 她身体前倾，好听清他说的话。

senses.definitionEn: Towards the future or from a particular time onwards.

example.en: From this point forward, keep a copy of every receipt.
example.zh: 从现在起，把每张收据都留一份。

senses.definitionEn: To send something you have received to another person or address.

example.en: Could you forward the email to me?
example.zh: 你能把邮件转发给我吗？

senses.definitionEn: Located near the front of something.

example.en: The forward section of the ship was damaged.
example.zh: 船的前部受损了。

senses.definitionEn: A player whose main role is to attack and score.

example.en: She plays as a forward for the school team.
example.zh: 她在校队踢前锋。

entries.orderingBasis: 优先排列常见用法，再列语域或专业义项。

entries.notes: play an instrument 指演奏乐器；measuring instruments 是测量仪器；an instrument of change 是推动变化的手段。

senses.definitionEn: An object used to make music.

example.en: The violin was the first instrument she learned to play.
example.zh: 小提琴是她学会演奏的第一种乐器。

senses.definitionEn: A tool designed for a precise task, such as measuring or operating.

example.en: The nurse checked that the surgical instruments were ready.
example.zh: 护士确认手术器械已经准备好。

senses.definitionEn: A means of bringing about a result.

example.en: Education can be an instrument of social change.
example.zh: 教育可以成为推动社会变革的手段。

senses.definitionEn: An asset or agreement with financial value that can often be traded.

example.en: A government bond is a financial instrument.
example.zh: 政府债券是一种金融工具。

entries.orderingBasis: 优先排列常见用法，再列语域或专业义项。

entries.notes: 名词用 access to；动词直接接宾语，如 access the files。表示一般意义的“使用权”时，access 通常不可数。

senses.definitionEn: The right or opportunity to use or obtain something.

example.en: Students have free access to the online library.
example.zh: 学生可以免费使用在线图书馆。

senses.definitionEn: A route or way of entering a place.

example.en: The bridge provides access to the island.
example.zh: 这座桥是通往岛上的通道。

senses.definitionEn: To open, retrieve or use information or a resource.

example.en: You can access the files from your phone.
example.zh: 你可以用手机访问这些文件。

senses.definitionEn: To reach or enter a place.

example.en: Visitors can access the garden through a side gate.
example.zh: 游客可以从侧门进入花园。

entries.orderingBasis: 优先排列常见用法，再列语域或专业义项。

entries.notes: 形容词和名词末尾通常读 /ət/，动词末尾读 /eɪt/。moderate exercise 指中等强度的运动；moderate a discussion 指主持讨论。

senses.definitionEn: Neither very large nor very small in amount or intensity.

example.en: We expect moderate growth this year.
example.zh: 我们预计今年会有适度增长。

senses.definitionEn: Avoiding extreme views, or a person who holds such views.

example.en: She takes a moderate position on the issue.
example.zh: 她在这个问题上的立场比较温和。

senses.definitionEn: To make or become less extreme, strong or severe.

example.en: Higher supply may help moderate prices.
example.zh: 供应增加可能有助于缓解价格上涨的压力。

senses.definitionEn: To guide a discussion or oversee what users post in a group.

example.en: She was asked to moderate the debate.
example.zh: 她受邀主持这场辩论。

entries.orderingBasis: 优先排列常见用法，再列语域或专业义项。

entries.notes: 英式 fish and chips 里的 chips 是薯条，美式 potato chips 通常是薯片。chip in 既可指凑钱，也可指插话。

senses.definitionEn: A small piece of semiconductor material containing an electronic circuit.

example.en: The new chip uses less power.
example.zh: 新芯片的耗电量更低。

senses.definitionEn: A small piece broken off a surface, or the mark left by it.

example.en: There is a chip in the rim of the cup.
example.zh: 杯沿有个缺口。

senses.definitionEn: A thin crisp slice of fried potato, or in British English a thicker fried strip.

example.en: We ordered fish and chips.
example.zh: 我们点了炸鱼薯条。

senses.definitionEn: A small token used in a game to represent money or points.

example.en: He placed two chips on the table.
example.zh: 他在桌上放了两枚筹码。

senses.meaningZh: 磕掉一小块；使出现缺口
senses.definitionEn: To break a small piece off something hard.

example.en: I chipped a tooth when I fell.
example.zh: 我摔倒时磕掉了一小块牙。

senses.definitionEn: To contribute money or add a comment to a conversation.

example.en: We each chipped in five dollars for the gift.
example.zh: 我们每人出了五美元买这件礼物。

entries.orderingBasis: 优先排列常见用法，再列语域或专业义项。

entries.notes: refresh the page 刷新页面；refresh your memory 帮你回想；refresh yourself 使自己恢复精神。

senses.definitionEn: To reload a page or display so that it shows current information.

example.en: Refresh the page to see the latest results.
example.zh: 刷新页面就能看到最新结果。

senses.meaningZh: 使恢复精神；使感到凉爽
senses.definitionEn: To make someone feel less tired or hot.

example.en: A quick shower refreshed me after the run.
example.zh: 跑完步后冲了个澡，我感觉精神多了。

senses.definitionEn: To help someone remember something again.

example.en: I reread my notes to refresh my memory.
example.zh: 我重读笔记，回想之前学过的内容。

senses.definitionEn: To update something so that it looks or feels new again.

example.en: They refreshed the design without changing the layout.
example.zh: 他们更新了设计，保留了原有布局。

entries.orderingBasis: 优先排列常见用法，再列语域或专业义项。

entries.notes: tuck A into B 表示把 A 塞进 B；tuck someone in 表示给某人掖好被子。英式口语 tuck into a meal 表示痛快地吃起来。

senses.definitionEn: To push the end of something into or under something else.

example.en: She tucked her shirt into her jeans.
example.zh: 她把衬衫下摆塞进牛仔裤里。

senses.definitionEn: To pull part of the body into a closer or smaller position.

example.en: Tuck your chin in slightly.
example.zh: 下巴稍微往里收一点。

senses.definitionEn: To make someone comfortable in bed by arranging the covers around them.

example.en: He tucked the children in before turning off the light.
example.zh: 他给孩子们掖好被子，然后关了灯。

senses.definitionEn: To put something in a safe or out-of-the-way place.

example.en: The cabin was tucked away among the trees.
example.zh: 小木屋隐在树林里。

senses.partOfSpeech: 短语动词 英式口语
senses.definitionEn: To start eating something with enthusiasm.

example.en: Everyone tucked into the noodles.
example.zh: 大家都津津有味地吃起了面条。

entries.orderingBasis: 优先排列常见用法，再列语域或专业义项。

entries.notes: snap at sb 常表示厉声说话，动物 snap at sth 则可能是突然张嘴去咬；snap a photo 是快速拍照；a snap decision 是仓促的决定。

senses.definitionEn: To break suddenly, often with a sharp sound.

example.en: The branch snapped under his weight.
example.zh: 树枝承受不住他的体重，啪地折断了。

senses.definitionEn: To move or close suddenly with a sharp sound.

example.en: The lid snapped shut.
example.zh: 盖子啪地合上了。

senses.definitionEn: To speak suddenly and angrily, or suddenly lose your temper.

example.en: I was tired and snapped at my brother.
example.zh: 我当时很累，冲弟弟嚷了一句。

senses.definitionEn: To try to bite something with a sudden movement of the jaws.

example.en: The dog snapped at the stick.
example.zh: 那条狗猛地朝棍子咬去。

senses.definitionEn: To take a quick photograph, or a photograph taken quickly.

example.en: She snapped a photo of the sunset.
example.zh: 她随手拍了一张日落照。

senses.definitionEn: Made suddenly and with little time for thought.

example.en: Try not to make a snap judgment.
example.zh: 尽量别匆忙下判断。

entries.orderingBasis: 优先排列常见用法，再列语域或专业义项。

entries.notes: contrive to do 表示经过努力或想办法做成某事；contrive a plan 表示设法想出计划。contrived 作形容词常指情节或安排牵强、不自然。

senses.definitionEn: To manage to do something, often despite difficulties.

example.en: They contrived to get the door open without a key.
example.zh: 他们没用钥匙也设法把门打开了。

senses.definitionEn: To devise a plan, device or method through ingenuity.

example.en: The engineer contrived a device to lift the heavy lid.
example.zh: 工程师想出了一个能抬起重盖子的装置。

senses.definitionEn: To arrange deliberately for something to happen.

example.en: He contrived a meeting between the two rivals.
example.zh: 他刻意安排了两个对手见面。

entries.orderingBasis: 优先排列常见用法，再列语域或专业义项。

entries.notes: a sore throat 是喉咙痛；sore muscles 是肌肉酸痛；be sore about sth 表示对某事心有不满。a sore spot 也可比喻敏感话题。

senses.definitionEn: Painful or tender, especially after use, injury or infection.

example.en: My legs were sore after the race.
example.zh: 比赛后我的腿很酸痛。

senses.definitionEn: A painful spot or open area on the skin or in the mouth.

example.en: She has a small sore inside her mouth.
example.zh: 她嘴里有一处小溃疡。

senses.definitionEn: Annoyed or upset about something.

example.en: He was still sore about losing the game.
example.zh: 他还在为输掉比赛而不高兴。

entries.orderingBasis: 优先排列常见用法，再列语域或专业义项。

entries.notes: flush with the wall 表示与墙面齐平；flush with cash 中的 flush 是“充裕的”；扑克牌 a flush 指同花牌型。

senses.definitionEn: To wash something away with a flow of water.

example.en: Flush the toilet after use.
example.zh: 用完厕所后请冲水。

senses.definitionEn: To become red in the face, or a sudden reddening of the skin.

example.en: Her cheeks flushed with embarrassment.
example.zh: 她尴尬得双颊通红。

senses.definitionEn: Level with an adjoining surface, without sticking out or sinking in.

example.en: The door sits flush with the wall.
example.zh: 门与墙面齐平。

senses.meaningZh: 资金充裕的；富有某物的
senses.definitionEn: Having plenty of money or of something else.

example.en: The company is flush with cash.
example.zh: 这家公司现金充足。

senses.definitionEn: To force a person or animal out of hiding.

example.en: The dogs flushed the birds out of the bushes.
example.zh: 狗把鸟从灌木丛里赶了出来。

senses.definitionEn: A poker hand with all its cards in the same suit.

example.en: She won the hand with a flush.
example.zh: 她以一手同花赢了这一局。

entries.orderingBasis: 优先排列常见用法，再列语域或专业义项。

entries.notes: daily routine 是日常作息；workout routine 是一套训练安排；routine check 是例行检查。

senses.definitionEn: A regular way of doing things or sequence of activities.

example.en: Reading before bed is part of my daily routine.
example.zh: 睡前阅读是我日常安排的一部分。

senses.definitionEn: Done regularly as part of a usual procedure.

example.en: The machine stopped during a routine check.
example.zh: 机器在一次例行检查中停了下来。

senses.definitionEn: A fixed sequence of movements or actions, especially in a performance.

example.en: The team practised its dance routine.
example.zh: 队员们练习了整套舞蹈动作。

senses.definitionEn: A set of instructions that performs a particular task in a program.

example.en: This routine checks whether the input is valid.
example.zh: 这个例程会检查输入是否有效。

entries.orderingBasis: 优先排列常见用法，再列语域或专业义项。

entries.notes: 动词变化为 stroke–stroked–stroked。a stroke of luck 是一次好运；a stroke of genius 是神来之笔；at a stroke 是一下子。heatstroke（也写作 heat stroke）指中暑，不能与脑卒中混淆。

senses.definitionEn: A sudden serious illness caused by a blockage or bleeding in the blood supply to the brain.

example.en: He had a stroke last year.
example.zh: 他去年中风了。

senses.definitionEn: To move your hand gently over a surface, or a gentle movement of this kind.

example.en: She stroked the cat's back.
example.zh: 她轻轻抚摸猫的背。

senses.definitionEn: A single movement used to hit a ball or strike something.

example.en: She won the point with a powerful stroke.
example.zh: 她以一记有力的击球赢下了这一分。

senses.meaningZh: 划水动作；游泳姿势；划桨动作
senses.definitionEn: A movement of the arms in swimming or of an oar in rowing; also, a swimming style.

example.en: He crossed the pool in twenty strokes.
example.zh: 他划了二十下游到了泳池另一端。

senses.definitionEn: A single movement of a pen, pencil or brush that leaves a mark.

example.en: The character has eight strokes.
example.zh: 这个字有八画。

senses.meaningZh: 一次意外的事；一次高明的举动
senses.definitionEn: A single unexpected event or an inspired action, especially in fixed phrases.

example.en: Finding the keys was a stroke of luck.
example.zh: 找到钥匙真是碰巧走运。

senses.meaningZh: 钟声的一响；报时的时刻
senses.definitionEn: A single sound of a striking clock, or the moment marked by it.

example.en: The show began on the stroke of midnight.
example.zh: 演出在午夜钟声敲响时开始。

entries.orderingBasis: 常见用法优先，固定搭配及报时义随后。

entries.notes: stiff muscles 是肌肉僵硬；a stiff drink 指烈酒；a stiff penalty 指严厉处罚。stiff upper lip 指遇事沉着、克制情绪。

senses.definitionEn: Difficult to bend or move freely.

example.en: My shoulders feel stiff after sitting all day.
example.zh: 坐了一整天后我的肩膀很僵硬。

senses.definitionEn: Formal or awkward in manner or style.

example.en: His stiff reply made the conversation awkward.
example.zh: 他生硬的回答让谈话变得尴尬。

senses.definitionEn: Strong or severe, especially of a challenge, price or penalty.

example.en: The team faces stiff competition.
example.zh: 这支队伍面临激烈的竞争。

senses.definitionEn: Firm and not easily bent.

example.en: The jacket has a stiff collar.
example.zh: 这件夹克的衣领很硬挺。

entries.orderingBasis: Common everyday senses first, then specialized or extended uses; editorial ordering, not a frequency claim.

entries.notes: 通常用复数 parameters 指规则或界限；within the parameters of the study 表示在研究范围内。数学或程序设计中，parameter 可指决定系统行为的参数，不等同于任何会变化的数值。

senses.definitionEn: A value that defines or affects the behaviour of a system or model.

example.en: Change the parameter to adjust the graph.
example.zh: 调整这个参数来改变图形。

senses.definitionEn: Limits or guidelines that determine what is allowed or possible.

example.en: We must work within the project's parameters.
example.zh: 我们必须在项目规定的范围内开展工作。

senses.definitionEn: A measurable factor used to describe a situation or system.

example.en: Temperature is an important parameter in the experiment.
example.zh: 温度是这项实验中的重要因素。

entries.orderingBasis: Common everyday senses first, then specialized or extended uses; editorial ordering, not a frequency claim.

entries.notes: tone of voice 是说话语气；muscle tone 是肌张力；tone down 表示使言辞或颜色柔和些。音乐中 a tone 可指音调，和 pitch 在具体用法上有区别。

senses.definitionEn: The attitude expressed by the way someone speaks or writes.

example.en: Her tone sounded calm and reassuring.
example.zh: 她的语气听起来平静而令人安心。

senses.definitionEn: A quality or pitch of a sound.

example.en: The instrument has a warm tone.
example.zh: 这件乐器的音色温暖。

senses.definitionEn: The general mood or character of a piece of writing or an event.

example.en: The opening sets a serious tone for the article.
example.zh: 开头为文章定下了严肃的基调。

senses.definitionEn: A particular shade or quality of a colour.

example.en: The room is decorated in soft blue tones.
example.zh: 房间用柔和的蓝色色调装饰。

senses.definitionEn: The normal firmness of a muscle, especially when it is at rest.

example.en: Regular movement can help maintain muscle tone.
example.zh: 规律活动有助于维持肌张力。

senses.definitionEn: To make muscles firmer, or make something less strong in tone.

example.en: The editor toned down the headline.
example.zh: 编辑把标题的措辞改得温和了一些。

entries.orderingBasis: Common everyday senses first, then specialized or extended uses; editorial ordering, not a frequency claim.

entries.definitionEn: As time passes; gradually over a period of time.
entries.usageEn: Describes a gradual change or development. It can appear at the beginning or end of a sentence.
entries.usageZh: 强调变化在一段时间内逐渐发生，常与 improve、change、develop、increase、decrease 等动词搭配，可放在句首或句末。

examples.en: Your English will improve over time.
examples.zh: 随着时间的推移，你的英语会逐渐进步。

examples.en: Over time, small changes can make a big difference.
examples.zh: 随着时间的推移，微小的变化也能带来很大的影响。

examples.en: The pattern becomes clearer over time.
examples.zh: 随着时间的推移，这个规律变得更加清晰。

entries.noteEn: Over time describes gradual change; in time means early enough or eventually; on time means at the scheduled time. Overtime (one word) means extra working time or extra time in a sports match.
entries.noteZh: over time 强调“随时间逐渐变化”；in time 表示“及时”或“最终”；on time 表示“准时”。注意 overtime 连写是另一个词，表示“加班（时间）”或“加时赛”。
